# A Rust file names what it exports and carries its own tests

> A test in the file it tests can read the private function it is testing, and moves with it when the file moves — which is the half of the convention no reviewer ever remembers to check.

Applies to `crates/*/src`.

<!-- archwarden:yours -->

## Context

_Everything between these two markers is yours. archwarden never rewrites it._

<!-- archwarden:end -->

## Considered and rejected

- **A sibling spec file, the way the webview does it** (nothing refuses it) — It cannot reach anything private, so it tests the crate's surface and calls it unit testing. The webview has sibling specs because TypeScript has no other option; Rust does.
- **A separate `tests/` directory** (nothing refuses it) — That is where integration tests belong and they exist too. A unit test put there stops being a unit test the moment it can only see `pub` items.
